title: Irreducible components under extension of the ground field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and $X$ a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $p:X_K\to X$ be the projection [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every irreducible component $T\subseteq |X|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], the inverse image $p^{-1}(T)$ is nonempty and is a union of irreducible components of $X_K$. For every irreducible component $C$ of $X_K$, the actual set-theoretic image $p(C)$ is an irreducible component of $X$; the map $C\mapsto p(C)$ is surjective onto the irreducible components of $X$. No finite-type, quasi-compactness, reducedness, algebraicity, or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 04KW (lemma-inverse-image-irreducible) and 04KX (lemma-image-irreducible); nonemptiness is stated in the final paragraph of the proof of 04KX.

proof.text: For any field extension E/F and F-scheme Y, the projection Y_E to Y is flat and surjective: apply flatness and surjectivity of Spec E to Spec F and their stability under base change. A component has a generic point by sobriety. In a scheme, a point is component-generic exactly when it has no proper generalization: a generalization of a component-generic point has irreducible closure containing that component, hence the same closure and the same point by sobriety; conversely place the closure of the point inside a component and use its generic point. We will use this criterion throughout. Each component-generic point w of Y_E maps to a component-generic point of Y: if z' is a generalization of z=r(w), generalizations lift along the flat map r, giving a generalization w' of w with r(w')=z'; the criterion gives w'=w, so z'=z, and the criterion makes z component-generic. These assertions apply without any finiteness assumptions.

source.place: Tags 04KW and 04KX, generic-point arguments; generalizations lift along flat morphisms, Morphisms Tag 03HV (lemma-generalizations-lift-flat)

proof.text: Fix a component T of X, with generic point eta. Choose a closed subscheme i:Z to X whose image is T. Its field base change Z_K to X_K is a closed immersion. Its image is exactly p^{-1}(T): one inclusion follows from the commuting square; for the converse a point w of X_K above t in T gives Spec kappa(w) to X factoring through Z. Indeed, locally i is Spec(A/I) to Spec A and the prime for t contains I, so A to kappa(w) kills I. Pair this factorization with Spec kappa(w) to Spec K in the fibre-product universal property. Thus |Z_K| is identified with p^{-1}(T). Flatness is not needed for this identification.

source.place: Tag 04KW, interpretation of T_K as the inverse image; Schemes Tags 01J3 and 01K1

proof.text: Let B be an irreducible component of Z_K and xi its generic point. Applying the generic-point image assertion from step 1 to the K/k extension of Z shows that xi maps to eta, since Z is irreducible. If xi' is a generalization of xi in X_K, its image generalizes eta. By the criterion of step 1, eta has no proper generalization in X, so p(xi')=eta and xi' lies in p^{-1}(T)=|Z_K|. The subspace topology of the closed immersion makes it a generalization there as well. Since xi is component-generic in Z_K, xi'=xi. The criterion now makes xi component-generic in X_K, and closedness of |Z_K| identifies the two closures of xi. Hence B is a component of X_K. The components cover Z_K, so p^{-1}(T) is a union of components of X_K. It is nonempty because p is surjective and T is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 04KW, entire proof; Tag 04KX, final paragraph

proof.text: First prove the image assertion when E/F is algebraic, for an arbitrary F-scheme Y. The map Spec E to Spec F is integral: an algebraic element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over a field, and division by its leading coefficient makes the equation monic. Its base change r:Y_E to Y is integral, hence universally closed, in particular closed. For a component B of Y_E with generic point xi, step 1 makes r(xi) component-generic in Y. Let T be its component. Continuity gives r(B) contained in the closure of {r(xi)}, namely T. Closedness of r gives the reverse inclusion since r(B) contains r(xi). Therefore the actual image r(B), not just its closure, equals T.

source.place: Tag 04KX, second proof paragraph; Morphisms Tags 01WL and 01WM

proof.text: For an algebraic extension E/F, the component map just constructed is surjective. Given a component T of Y, steps 2--3 give a nonempty union of components inside r^{-1}(T). Choose one, B. Step 4 makes r(B) a component, and r(B) is contained in T. Maximality of an irreducible component forces r(B)=T. This argument also covers algebraic extensions of infinite degree.

We also need the component bijection over a separably closed field F. If E/F is any extension and Y is an F-scheme, the fibre of r:Y_E to Y at y is Spec(kappa(y) tensor_F E): compose the fibre-product universal properties and then use the affine-spectrum tensor description. The field-tensor lemma makes this fibre irreducible and nonempty because F is separably closed. The scheme-theoretic fibre has the topology of r^{-1}(y), and r is open because schemes over a field are universally open. The continuous open-map theorem with irreducible fibres therefore gives mutually inverse maps B maps to r(B) and T maps to r^{-1}(T) on components. In particular these are actual images. This proves the comparison needed below using the existing tensor and topological lemmas, rather than introducing a node for a clause of the item.

source.place: Tag 04KX, first proof paragraph, using Tag 038F and lemma-separably-closed-field-irreducible-components; Algebra Tag 00I7

proof.text: Return to arbitrary K/k. Choose an algebraic closure Omega of K and let A be the subfield of elements of Omega algebraic over k. The relative-algebraic-closure lemma makes A algebraically closed, hence separably closed: a nonconstant polynomial splits into linear factors by successive root extraction and division, so in particular every separable polynomial splits. We have compatible inclusions k into A into Omega and K into Omega. Write a:X_Omega to X_K, b:X_Omega to X_A, and c:X_A to X. Fibre-product functoriality gives p composed with a = c composed with b. For a component C of X_K, step 5 for the algebraic extension Omega/K provides a component D of X_Omega with a(D)=C. Step 6 over A makes b(D) a component of X_A. Step 4 for the algebraic extension A/k makes c(b(D)) a component of X. The commuting equality gives p(C)=p(a(D))=c(b(D)), proving the actual-image assertion for every C.

source.place: Tag 04KX, first proof paragraph, with algebraic closures instead of separable closures; Fields Tags 09GT, 09GJ and 09GR

proof.text: Finally, for a component T of X choose a component C contained in the nonempty union p^{-1}(T) from step 3. Step 7 makes p(C) a component of X contained in T, so maximality gives p(C)=T. Thus C maps to p(C) is a well-defined surjection on components. If X is empty, both component sets are empty and the assertion about individual T is vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Tags 04KW and 04KX, proofs; the comparison square uses algebraic closures in place of separable algebraic closures.
